prompt: How do I number pages starting from the second page in Word?
completion:
**Short answer**

1. Insert a *section break* after the first page.  
2. Edit the header/footer of the new section.  
3. Turn off “Link to Previous”.  
4. Delete the number that appears on the first page (or check “Different First Page”).  
5. Insert a page number in the second‑page header/footer.  
6. Set the numbering to start at **1** (not at the document‑wide default).

---

## Step‑by‑step for the most common Word versions

> **Tip:** The process is essentially the same in Word 2010, 2013, 2016, 2019, 2021, Office 365 and on Word for Mac.  
> If you’re on an older version (2007 or earlier) the labels are slightly different but the steps are identical.

| What to do | Word 2016‑2021 (Windows) | Word 2016‑2021 (Mac) | Word 2007 |
|------------|--------------------------|---------------------|-----------|
| 1. **Place cursor** at the end of the first page (after any title, preface, etc.) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| 2. **Insert a section break** (next page) | `Layout` → `Breaks` → `Section Breaks` → `Next Page` | `Insert` → `Breaks` → `Section Break` → `Next Page` | `Page Layout` → `Breaks` → `Section Breaks` → `Next Page` |
| 3. **Open the header/footer** of the new section | Double‑click the top or bottom margin (or `Insert` → `Header`/`Footer`) | Double‑click the header/footer | Double‑click the header/footer |
| 4. **Turn off “Link to Previous”** | Design tab → **Link to Previous** (uncheck) | Design tab → **Link to Previous** (uncheck) | Design tab → **Link to Previous** (uncheck) |
| 5. **Remove the number on page 1** | Either delete the number manually **or** check `Different First Page` in the Design tab | Check `Different First Page` (removes the number automatically) | Check `Different First Page` (removes the number automatically) |
| 6. **Insert the page number** in the second‑page header/footer | `Insert` → `Page Number` → choose position & style | `Insert` → `Page Number` → choose position & style | `Insert` → `Page Number` → choose position & style |
| 7. **Start numbering at 1** | Click the inserted number → Design tab → `Format Page Numbers…` → set **Start at** → `1` | Click the inserted number → Format → `Format Page Numbers…` → set **Start at** → `1` | Click the inserted number → `Page Number Format…` → set **Start at** → `1` |

---

## Detailed walk‑through (Windows)

1. **Create the section break**  
   *Place your cursor at the very end of the first page.*  
   ```Layout → Breaks → Section Breaks → Next Page```

2. **Edit the header/footer**  
   *Double‑click the top or bottom margin of page 2 (or click `Insert → Header` / `Footer`).*  
   This opens the Header & Footer Tools – **Design** tab.

3. **Break the link**  
   In the Design tab click the **Link to Previous** button so that it is **unchecked**.  
   This stops the header/footer from mirroring the first section.

4. **Hide the first‑page number**  
   *Option A:* Delete the number that appears on page 1 (it may be a placeholder).  
   *Option B:* In the Design tab tick **Different First Page** – Word will automatically suppress the number on page 1.

5. **Insert the number on page 2**  
   In the header/footer of page 2 click **Insert → Page Number → Bottom of Page (or Top, as you wish)** → choose a style.

6. **Set the starting page**  
   Click the newly inserted page‑number field → Design tab → **Format Page Numbers…** → choose **Start at:** `1`.  
   Click **OK**.  
   Now page 2 shows “1”, page 3 shows “2”, and so on.

---

## Detailed walk‑through (Mac)

1. `Insert → Breaks → Section Break (next page)`  
2. Double‑click header/footer → Design tab appears.  
3. Untick **Link to Previous**.  
4. Tick **Different First Page** (the number on page 1 disappears).  
5. Insert page number on page 2 (`Insert → Page Number → Bottom of Page`).  
6. Click the number → Format → **Start at:** `1` → Done.

---

## If you already have page numbers on the whole document

If your document already has page numbers that start from 1 on the title page and you want to change that:

1. Follow the steps above to insert a *section break* after the first page.  
2. Go back to the first page header/footer, delete the number (or use “Different First Page”).  
3. Insert the page numbers in the new section and format them to start at 1.

---

## Quick‑fix: Use “Different First Page”

If you only need the *first page* to be blank but still want the rest to be numbered automatically (no manual start‑at adjustment), simply:

1. `Insert → Page Number` (any position).  
2. Go to the first page header/footer.  
3. In the Design tab check **Different First Page**.  
4. Delete the number that appears on that page.  

Word will then display the numbers starting on the second page without any extra numbering configuration.

---

### Common pitfalls

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| Page number still appears on the first page | Make sure **Link to Previous** is off AND **Different First Page** is ticked (or delete the number manually). |
| Number starts at 0 or 3 | In the header/footer click the number → **Format Page Numbers…** → set **Start at** = `1`. |
| Number format changes when you insert more sections | Each section’s numbering can be formatted independently. Re‑apply the `Start at 1` setting in the new section’s header/footer. |

---

## Summary

- Insert a **section break** after the page that you want unnumbered.  
- Turn off **Link to Previous** (or enable **Different First Page**).  
- Delete the number from the first page if it appears.  
- Insert the number in the second page’s header/footer and set it to start at **1**.  

That’s it! Your document will now number pages starting from the second page.
